rv.q: I'd go so far as to say this is the most powerful non-Equity production, all in all, I've seen since before the pandemic either wrecked or compromised so many of our small Chicago theater companies.
Ambitious, compassionate, and unflinching, this production captures the emotional sweep and political fury that make Tony Kushner’s masterpiece as vital now as it was in the 1990s.
Their staging not only honors Kushner’s towering vision but also transforms it into something urgent and immediate.

Invictus’s imaginatively staged, crisply paced, and beautifully performed and designed realization of this durable American masterpiece is genuinely entertaining and moving, as well as intellectually stimulating.

Seen together, the two parts are best described in a word: Epic. “Angels” is three stories woven together, and director Charles Askenaizer proves to be a capable weaver. The set is an upscale law office that looks to have suffered a bomb blast, with the words “In _ We Trust” inscribed on an entablature above a desk, and a burnt and ragged U.S.
And like a great work of public art, this theatrical achievement is urgent and timeless and a gift to us all.
Invictus’ production feels true to the original play and themes that strike a chord to the happenings of today.

cn.t: Critics hail Invictus Theatre's production as bold, pitch-perfect storytelling that honors Kushner's epic masterpiece with compelling performances and top-tier design, proving off-Loop theater's triumphant return.
